Oni Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Oni, Georgia

Not demolished. Oni's Jewish community, documented from the early 18th century, grew to 3,000 residents by the 1880s - about half the town's population - and peaked at 3,500 before mass emigration to Israel between 1972 and 1992 left only about 10 Jews today. Oni's Great Synagogue, Georgia's third-largest after Tbilisi and Kutaisi, was built 1890-1895 in Neo-Moorish style with financial backing arranged through Nathan Rothschild and Alfred Nobel, after young Rabbi Elia Amshikashvili was inspired by Warsaw's Great Synagogue. During 1930s Soviet religious repression, Jewish and Georgian mothers reportedly saved the building by locking themselves inside with their newborns. The original 1890s synagogue was destroyed in a 1991 earthquake; the Great Synagogue survived and was repaired. From 1903, community rabbi David Baazov opened Jewish schools and, in 1919, a yeshiva; he also founded Georgia's first Zionist group in 1910, leading to his exile to Siberia (1938-1945). His son Herzel Baazov, a noted playwright, was executed for dissent in 1938. This older cemetery's tombstones are mostly uninscribed, with the one legible inscription suggesting a 19th or early 20th century date. A Holocaust and Righteous Among the Nations memorial (honoring Sergey Metreveli) was unveiled here in 2020.
